CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository. Claude code was initially used from within the Desktop App as a coworker project and is also used integrated within the Positron IDE - make sure both can read all files within this directory.

Package Overview

mesoclim is an R package for mechanistic downscaling of climate data from coarse (10s km) to fine (<1 km) spatial resolution and from daily to hourly temporal resolution. It handles ERA5 reanalysis data and UKCP18 climate model projections. The primary effects captured by the methods are the effects of terrain (slope,aspect,elevation) on climate variables. The package does not model the effects of landcover or vegetation. The functions (at least the higher level functions) seek to allow a range of different data formats in particular spatraster, numeric arrays and vectors. Rccp C++ functions are used for some of the most computationally intensive calculations.

The package supplies both vignettes and (largely identical) articles on the package web pages.

Structure of directories

The subdirectories follow standard R package guidance and use, such as subdirectory R/ contains source files, with following additions: (i) The subdirectory raw_data_files contains some raw data not for climate in package (ii) The subdirectory analyses vcontains various workflows and analyses not for inclusion in package. (iii) The subdirectory R_new is for containing any new R code I think might be used but not for inclusion in the package.

These additional subdirectories can be read but should not be modified without explicit approval.

Standard workflow and use

  1. Prepare coarse resolution climate data (ERA5 or UKCP18RCM) to standard climdata format
  2. Prepare ancillary data: digital elevation models (dtms) at fine and coarse resolution, land/sea masks, sea-surface temperatures
  3. Bias correction against observational data (HadUK-Grid) at coarse resolution
  4. Spatial and/or temporal downscaling

Commenting , Testing and Publication

Keep any new code comments to a minimum and very concise, and only remove existing code comments if the comment isn’t relevant anymore. Use roxygen comments as the primary means to comment on code.

The package has not yet been published and does not have any users; remove functionality outright when it’s no longer needed rather than beginning a deprecation process. No need to worry about breaking changes.

Intention is to publish to github and a package github page with articles. No plans as yet to publish to CRAN.

The package could do with much more robust testing procedures.

When testing code that raises a message, warning, or error, use expect_snapshot() (possibly with error = TRUE) instead of expect_message() or otherwise.

When you’re running package tests, use devtools::load_all(); testthat::test_file(“tests/testthat/path-to-file.R”). If you encounter namespacing issues, don’t delete tests that otherwise should work, and instead ask me what to do.

Related Packages

The package re-uses many functions from (and aims to be losely compatible/familiar to) the following github packages: https://github.com/ilyamaclean/micropoint https://github.com/ilyamaclean/microclimf https://github.com/ilyamaclean/microclimmdata https://github.com/ilyamaclean/terravars https://github.com/ilyamaclean/microclimlearn

Development Commands

# Install dependencies and build package
devtools::install_deps()
devtools::build()

# Load package for interactive development (faster than install)
devtools::load_all()

# Run all tests
devtools::test()

# Run a single test file
testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-workerfunctions.R")

# Generate documentation from roxygen2 comments
devtools::document()

# Check package for CRAN compliance
devtools::check()

# Compile C++ code (Rcpp) — run after any change to src/mesoclimCpp.cpp
Rcpp::compileAttributes()
devtools::build(compile_attributes = TRUE)

After modifying C++ files in src/, always run Rcpp::compileAttributes() to regenerate R/RcppExports.R and src/RcppExports.cpp before testing.

pkgdown site

Site is published at https://ilyamaclean.github.io/mesoclim from the gh-pages branch of ilyamaclean/mesoclim. To rebuild and redeploy (run from RStudio — needs its bundled pandoc):

pkgdown::deploy_to_branch()   # builds docs/ and pushes to gh-pages

docs/ is gitignored — never commit it. The _pkgdown.yml controls the reference index (explicit contents: lists) and article order.

Architecture

Standard “climdata” Format

All climate data is standardised into a named list: - dtm: a SpatRaster of the elevation grid (at climate model resolution) - tme: vector of POSIXct timestamps - windheight_m, tempheight_m: measurement heights (numeric) - Named numeric arrays [x, y, time] for: tmin, tmax, temp, relhum, spechum, pres, swrad, lwrad, windspeed, winddir, prec

Functions in data_functions.R handle I/O (read_climdata, write_climdata) and validation (checkinputs).

Processing Pipeline

  1. Input conversion (era5_functions.R, ukcp_functions.R): NetCDF → climdata list
  2. Spatial downscaling (spatialdownscale.R, workerfunctions.R): elevation lapse rate, coastal exposure, cold-air drainage, wind shelter, terrain shading
  3. Temporal downscaling (temporaldownscale.R): daily → hourly via physically-based diurnal curves
  4. Bias correction (biascorrect_functions.R): quantile-mapping against HadUK-Grid
  5. Large-domain tiling (tile_functions.R): overlapping tiles for memory management

File Responsibilities

File Purpose
spatialdownscale.R Public spatial downscaling wrappers: spatialdownscale, spatialdownscale_tiles, winddownscale, precipdownscale, swdownscale, lwdownscale, presdownscale, relhumdownscale, tempdaily_downscale, temphrly_downscale
temporaldownscale.R Daily→hourly: *_dailytohourly, subdailyrain, temporaldownscale
climatefunctions.R Physical models: calculate_terrain_shading (skyview + horizon; skyview_only flag; steps=36), clearskyrad, difprop, lapserate, coastalexposure, windelev, calculate_windcoeffs, converthumidity, daylength
workerfunctions.R ~50 internal helpers (dot-prefixed): type conversions, spatial interpolation, terrain, cold-air drainage (basindelin, flowacc), landfill_climdata, get_dem
biascorrect_functions.R biascorrect / biascorrect_apply / biascorrect_climdata / precipcorrect / precipcorrect_apply. biascorrect_climdata handles partial model lists (warns and skips missing variables rather than stopping)
era5_functions.R ERA5 NetCDF → climdata
ukcp_functions.R UKCP18 NetCDF → climdata. Dot-functions are internal (@noRd), not exported
data_functions.R I/O, validation (checkinputs), plotting, subset_climdata, landfill_climdata
tile_functions.R create_overlapping_tiles, tiled processing
data.R Dataset roxygen documentation only

C++ Acceleration (src/mesoclimCpp.cpp)

Called via Rcpp wrappers in R/RcppExports.R:

Function Purpose
basinCpp(dm2, bsn, method) Basin delineation — O(N log N) min-heap (replaced O(N²) scan). method="any" or "steepest"
basinmerge_cpp(dm2, bm2, boundary) Basin merging — pour-point scan + union-find (single-pass transitive merge)
fill_land_na_idw(temp, landMask) Fill NA land cells by IDW from neighbours (used by landfill_climdata)
hourlytempv / hourlytempm Daily→hourly temperature (vector/matrix)
clearskyradmCpp Clear-sky solar radiation matrix
difpropmCpp Diffuse/direct radiation partitioning
rainadjustv / rainadjustm Precipitation temporal disaggregation
hourtodayCpp Hourly→daily aggregation
renumberbasin Renumber basin IDs to 1:N

STL headers required for basin code: <string>, <queue>, <unordered_map>, <functional>. Compiled artefacts (*.o, *.so, *.dll) are gitignored — never commit them.

Internal Conventions

  • Internal functions are dot-prefixed (.resample(), .spatinterp(), .tempelev() etc.)
  • Dot-functions should not have @export — use @noRd to suppress .Rd generation
  • Public functions that are part of the API should have @export, @keyword, and @examples \dontrun{}
  • Data type helpers: .is() (SpatRaster→array), .rta() (raster→array), .vta() (vector→array), .rast() (array→SpatRaster)
  • Functions accept both terra::SpatRaster and legacy raster objects
  • PackedSpatRaster used for serialisation (write_climdata / read_climdata)

R dependencies

Environment

  • Local R is 4.3.3 (arm64). CRAN no longer ships macOS binaries for some newer packages on 4.3, so they build from source; Rust (brew install rust) is installed for packages such as yaml12.
  • The r-btw MCP server (btw::btw_mcp_server(tools = 'docs')) is available. Use its tools to read installed help pages, vignettes and NEWS instead of guessing function signatures. Its mesoclim help reflects the installed build, which may lag the source in R/.

Core: terra

  • Almost all spatial code uses terra, called explicitly as terra:: (~270 calls in R/). Write new code the same way.
  • SpatRaster/SpatVector objects hold C++ pointers and cannot be saveRDS’d or stored in package data directly. Use terra::wrap() / terra::unwrap() (see write_climdata / read_climdata).
  • Prefer terra idioms: rast (not raster/brick/stack), app (not calc), global (not cellStats), project (not projectRaster), classify (not reclassify), ext (not extent), nlyr (not nlayers).
  • Behaviour differs from raster: values() always returns a matrix. mean(x, y) is computed layer-wise (use mean(c(x, y)) for an overall mean). Bilinear resample() differs at edges. The internal .resample() wraps terra::resample with NA removal.

raster

  • Still in Imports with import(raster), but only one brick( call remains. Functions still accept legacy raster objects as input; don’t add new raster calls. Full import of both raster and terra can mask generics, so qualify calls with terra::.

Other Imports and their roles

Package Role in mesoclim
fields Thin-plate spline downscaling (Tpsdownscale: Tps / fastTps)
gstat IDW spatial interpolation (gstat/idw)
mgcv GAM fits (gam)
zoo Temporal NA interpolation (na.approx)
fmsb Radar charts in plot_wind (radarchart)
ncdf4 Reading UKCP18 / ERA5 / SST netCDF files
lubridate Date/time handling for tme vectors
sf, units Vector geometry / CRS and unit handling alongside terra
curl, elevatr Used only by get_dem; drop them if get_dem is removed
abind Not used anywhere; candidate for removal
magrittr %>% pipe (vignettes and some internals)
Rcpp Compiled helpers in src/mesoclimCpp.cpp (see C++ section above)

grDevices, graphics and stats appear in NAMESPACE importFrom() but not in DESCRIPTION Imports:, so R CMD check warns.

Undeclared / optional

  • microclima:: is referenced once in R/ but is not in DESCRIPTION.
  • HyetosMinute (sub-daily rainfall, R/temporaldownscale.R) must be attached with library() because it calls C++ code; it is not on CRAN and is not declared.

Suggests

knitr, rmarkdown (vignettes in vignettes/), and testthat (edition 3, tests in tests/testthat/).
